content.text: All responsive locations reviewed: §14 (ownership/assignment, joint ownership, feedback), §15 (Customer Data), §13.2 (embedded Vendor Technology licence), and the definitions of "Deliverable", "Customer Data" and "Vendor Technology". No assignment or licence of our IP/data to the Vendor beyond processing to deliver the Services; no aggregated-data or feedback grab.

input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets our preferred position in full. §14.2 gives us ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for us and contains an express present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest, backed by personnel assignments and further-assurance. §14.3 confirms Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, which is defined at 1.9 as its pre-existing software, tools, models, templates and technology and expressly excludes Customer Data and IP we owned before the Effective Date; §14.3 cross-refers to §13.2, which grants us and our Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from" material embedded in a Deliverable. §14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right, and §15.1 bars sale, advertising use, commingling and model training. §14.4 provides that no jointly owned IP is created absent a separately signed instrument that identifies exploitation rights, and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. Two points short of ideal drafting are noted rather than flagged: §13.2 extends the licence to contractors supporting our business rather than granting a general sublicensing right (a fallback-only element), and §13.3 permits suspension of a licence during a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and cure, which slightly qualifies irrevocability. Neither is material and neither warrants a redline.
